Scope: Bounded imported-Wikitext template dependency resolution and diagnostic hardening; not historical MediaWiki parity.
AuditedComponents: MediaWikiTemplateExpander expansion state and active dependency chain
TwMediaWikiTemplateTarget resolution status and source-body contract

Findings.Evidence: The import schema preserves full OriginalTitle values such as Template:Example, while the expander supplies the namespace-stripped title. The resolver now normalizes explicit Template: input and matches both stored bare and full forms under namespace 10.
A synthetic repository exception previously escaped RenderAsync. It now yields sanitized TemplateResolutionFailed, ResolutionFailed dependency evidence, and terminal first-cause preservation.

Findings.Area: Resolved target without source body or identity
Findings.Evidence: A Resolved target with unavailable source data was previously mapped to MissingTemplate. It now yields TemplateSourceUnavailable.

Synthetic revisions verify an exact eligible timestamp, future exclusion, and selection by timestamp rather than revision-ID order. MySQL uses the same <= timestamp predicate and deterministic timestamp/target-revision ordering.
Direct, transitive, diamond, repeated, self, multi-node, and parser-function cycle fixtures terminate deterministically without false repeated-dependency cycles.
Unselected missing templates and cycles are not requested by #if/#ifeq/#switch fixtures.
The existing bounded subset diagnoses these forms and does not silently reinterpret a main-namespace page or invent aliases.

The current template status contract exposes Restricted but not separate deleted, suppressed, or no-eligible-revision states. The resolver's SQL filters those rows fail-closed without inferring a more specific cause.

RecommendedNextMilestone: Run the corrected resolver against an explicitly authorized disposable MariaDB import containing complete historical template bodies, then reconcile real render provenance separately from worker certification and Cargo parity.
